title: Girls Circle Skirt Sewing Pattern – Free PDF
content:
Garment Girls full circle skirt with fly zipper

Level Easy (confident beginner)

Sizes US 2 – 18 (height 91 – 165 cm)

Fabric Cotton poplin, chambray, light denim, twill, linen

Pieces 6

This free girls circle skirt sewing pattern makes a full, twirly skirt that closes at the front with a real fly zipper and a button, just like a pair of jeans. The waistband stays flat at the front and has elastic in the back, so the skirt is comfortable at school, gives a little room to grow and is easy for her to put on alone.

Print page 1 at 100% and check that the test square measures 10 cm (4 in). New to PDF patterns? Read how to print and assemble a PDF pattern.

Sizing guide

Choose the size from the child’s waist measurement, not from her age. If the waist and the height point to different sizes, go by the waist and adjust the length at the hem. The elastic in the back waistband stretches, so the skirt fits anywhere between the “elastic relaxed” and “open flat” waist below. Not sure how to measure? Read how to take body measurements and how to choose your size.

Kids sizes: US 2 to 18, drafted for a height of 91 to 165 cm. US sizes are a guide only, always choose by measurements.

Body measurements

Finished skirt measurements

Skirt length is measured at the side, from the top of the waistband to the hem. Hem width is the full circumference of the hem: that is what makes the skirt twirl.

Fabric amounts

Estimated by laying out all pieces for the largest size of each group, single layer, plus 8 % for shrinkage. A circle skirt needs a lot of width, so 150 cm wide fabric is much more economical for the bigger sizes. Fusible interfacing: 0.2 m, any width.

Zipper and elastic

Elastic to cut = the length printed on the waistband piece + 2 cm (1 cm at each end to stitch it down). A longer zipper is fine: you shorten it in step 2.

Common fit adjustments

Length. Each size is drafted for the height in the chart. To lengthen or shorten, add or remove the same amount all around the hem of the fronts and the back, following the curve.

Growing room. Between two sizes, choose by the waist and simply leave the skirt a little longer: a circle skirt still looks good when it is worn a season later.

Materials

  • Main fabric: 1.2 to 1.7 m (1 3/8 to 1 7/8 yd) of 150 cm wide light to medium woven fabric with a soft drape: cotton poplin, chambray, light denim (4–6 oz), cotton twill, linen or viscose twill
  • Fly zipper: a metal or nylon jeans zipper, 16 cm for sizes 2–6 and 18 cm for sizes 7–18 (a longer one can be shortened)
  • Elastic: woven or knitted, 2.5 cm wide for sizes 2–5 and 3 cm for sizes 6–18
  • Button: 1 button of 1 cm (3/8″)
  • Interfacing: 0.2 m of light fusible interfacing
  • Matching thread, a safety pin, chalk or a washable pen

Pattern pieces

  • 1 Skirt front: cut 2 (one left, one right, mirrored)
  • 2 Skirt back: cut 1, single layer
  • 3 Waistband: cut 1
  • 4 Fly facing (fly shield): cut 1
  • 5 Fly interfacing: cut 1 in fusible interfacing
  • 6 Waistband interfacing: cut 2 in fusible interfacing

Cut the left front only along the line marked CUT ON LEFT FRONT: it keeps a narrow extension for the zipper, the right front keeps the wide one that becomes the fly. The back is drawn whole: cut it on a single layer, not on the fold.

Design details of the girls circle skirt

The Girls Circle Skirt is a full circle skirt with a grown-up detail: a real topstitched fly front. In our photo it is sewn in a rust cotton twill and worn with a simple white tee and knee socks, but it is just as cute in chambray, light denim or a small print.

  • Full circle skirt: two quarter-circle fronts and a half-circle back, for maximum twirl
  • Front seam with a fly zipper and a fly shield behind it
  • Curved topstitched fly, like on jeans
  • Waistband flat at the front with one button, elastic in the back for comfort
  • Side seams with matching notches
  • Narrow 5 mm machine hem that follows the curve

The fly zipper is the only tricky part, and it is explained one small step at a time. Everything else (side seams, waistband, hem) is quick, so it is a lovely first project with a zipper.

Sewing notes

Fit & style

Fitted at the waist, very full at the hem. Choose the size by the waist and adjust the length.

Fabrics

Light to medium woven fabrics with a soft drape. Avoid stretch fabric and very stiff fabric.

Cutting & sewing

Staystitch the bias waist right after cutting and hang the skirt for 24 hours before hemming.

Choosing fabric for a girls circle skirt

A circle skirt is cut mostly on the bias, so it loves fabrics with a soft drape: cotton poplin, chambray, light denim of 4 to 6 oz, cotton twill, linen or a linen blend and viscose twill all work well. A medium fabric like twill gives a nice full shape, a lighter poplin or viscose falls in softer folds.

Avoid very stiff fabrics, which make the circle stand out like a bell, and stretch fabrics: the fly zipper and the flat front waistband need a stable fabric. Wash and dry your fabric before cutting, because children’s skirts are washed often.

Sewing steps

Seam allowance 1 cm (3/8″) unless stated otherwise. Finish raw edges with a serger or a zigzag stitch and press every seam as you go. “Left” and “right” always mean as worn.

  1. Prepare the pieces. Fuse the fly interfacing to the wide extension of the right front and the two waistband interfacings to the ends of the waistband. Staystitch the waist edges 6 mm from the edge and finish the front and side edges.
  2. Shorten the zipper. If needed, mark the new stop at the circle on the front seam, whipstitch across the teeth and cut 2 cm below.
  3. Front seam. Sew the two fronts together from the hem up to the circle, then baste the opening closed up to the waist.
  4. Zipper. Fold the narrow left extension, stitch the zipper under the fold, then stitch the other tape to the wide right extension only.
  5. Topstitch the fly. Draw the curved fly line about 2.5 to 3 cm from the centre front, topstitch it through the right front and the extension, and remove the basting.
  6. Fly shield. Fold the fly facing, stitch it behind the zipper on the left side and bar tack at the bottom of the curve.
  7. Side seams. Sew the fronts to the back at the sides, matching the notches, without stretching the fabric.
  8. Prepare the waistband. Press under one long edge and stitch the stretched elastic on the inner half, between the two ELASTIC marks.
  9. Attach the waistband. Sew it to the skirt, matching the side seam and centre back marks, close the ends and the underlap, turn it and stitch the inside edge down.
  10. Secure the elastic. Stitch through all layers at the elastic ends and topstitch along the back waistband.
  11. Buttonhole and button. Make a 1.2 cm horizontal buttonhole on the right end and sew the button on the underlap.
  12. Hem. Let the skirt hang for 24 hours, level the hem, then sew a narrow 5 mm + 5 mm hem.

Tips and common mistakes

Stretched waist. The waist edge is on the bias: staystitch it right after cutting and do not pull the fabric while sewing.

Uneven hem. Always hang the skirt for a day before hemming so the bias can drop, then trim the hem level.

Wavy fly. Use the interfacing on the fly extension and draw the topstitching line with chalk before you sew.

Waistband too tight. Cut the elastic to the length in the table: the back should gather softly, not bunch up.

How to style the girls circle skirt

School and everyday: in rust twill with a white tee and knee socks, like in our photo.

Winter: in denim or needlecord with a fitted long-sleeve top, tights and boots.

Party: in a soft viscose with a cardigan and ballet flats.

Want a full matching look? Sew our girls puff sleeve dress sewing pattern in the same size range, or make a grown-up version with the A-line denim skirt sewing pattern.

Care

Wash at 30 °C inside out with the zipper closed, avoid a hot tumble dryer (the elastic does not like it) and press on the wrong side.

Questions

Is seam allowance included?

Yes: 1 cm (3/8″) everywhere, and the hem allowance is 1 cm (3/8″), sewn as a narrow 5 mm + 5 mm hem.

Which paper sizes are included?

The free download comes in A4 and US Letter, as a printable PDF with one file per size, US 2 to 18.

Which size should I choose?

Choose by the child’s waist measurement. If the waist and the height point to different sizes, go by the waist and adjust the length.

Is this skirt good for beginners?

Yes, for a confident beginner. The only tricky part is the fly zipper (steps 3 to 6); the paid tutorial has illustrations and video guides for it.

Can I use a stretch fabric?

No, the fly zipper and the flat front waistband need a stable woven fabric.

How much fabric does a circle skirt need?

From 1.2 m to 1.7 m of 150 cm wide fabric, depending on the size. With 115 cm wide fabric, the bigger sizes need almost twice as much.
